title: The 80-Year Answer: Why Friends Are Not Optional
title_zh: 八十年的答案：朋友为何不可或缺
intro_zh: 本文约920词，围绕友谊对健康与幸福的影响展开，包含哈佛成人发展研究、孤独的危害、蓝区事例以及维护友谊的简单方法。

paragraphs.en: For more than eighty years, a study at Harvard University has followed the same group of people, asking them about their lives every two years. The project began in 1938 with 724 men. Some were Harvard students; others were boys from poor neighborhoods in Boston. Researchers checked their health, jobs, and marriages. They asked about their friendships. The study is now run by Robert Waldinger, who often shares one clear finding: good relationships keep us happier and healthier. 'The only thing that really matters in life are your relationships to other people,' said George Vaillant, a former director. This is not a greeting card message. It is a scientific result.
paragraphs.zh: 八十多年来，哈佛大学的一项研究一直追踪同一组人，每两年询问他们的生活状况。该项目始于1938年，有724名男性参与。有些是哈佛学生，有些是波士顿贫困社区的男孩。研究人员检查他们的健康、工作和婚姻，也询问他们的友谊。这项研究现在由罗伯特·沃尔丁格负责，他经常分享一个明确的发现：良好的人际关系让我们更快乐、更健康。前主任乔治·瓦兰特曾说：‘生活中唯一真正重要的是你与他人的关系。’这不是一张贺卡上的话，而是一个科学结论。

paragraphs.en: The data are surprisingly specific. When researchers looked at the men at age 50, they found that satisfaction with relationships was a better predictor of physical health at age 80 than cholesterol levels. In other words, how happy you are with your friends and family may matter more than how much you exercise or what you eat. Another study from Brigham Young University reviewed 148 studies and found that people with strong social ties had a 50 percent higher chance of living longer than those with weak ties. Loneliness, on the other hand, is not just a sad feeling. It is a serious risk factor.
paragraphs.zh: 数据出人意料地具体。当研究人员观察这些男性50岁时的状况时，他们发现，对人际关系的满意度比胆固醇水平更能预测80岁时的身体健康。换句话说，你对朋友和家人的满意程度，可能比锻炼多少或吃什么更重要。杨百翰大学的另一项研究回顾了148项研究，发现社会关系强的人比关系弱的人长寿几率高50%。另一方面，孤独不仅仅是一种悲伤的感觉，它还是一个严重的风险因素。

paragraphs.en: Scientists have compared loneliness to smoking fifteen cigarettes a day. That is a significant claim, but it comes from careful research. Lonely people tend to have higher levels of stress hormones, weaker immune systems, and poorer sleep. Over time, these effects increase the risk of heart disease, memory loss, and even early death. One study found that lonely adults were 26 percent more likely to die during a seven-year period than those who felt connected. The opposite is also true: good friends can help us recover from illness faster and handle stress better. Friendship, it seems, is not a luxury. It is a basic need, like food and water.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家把孤独比作每天抽十五支烟。这是一个重大的论断，但它来自严谨的研究。孤独的人往往压力激素水平更高、免疫系统更弱、睡眠更差。随着时间推移，这些影响会增加心脏病、记忆丧失甚至早逝的风险。一项研究发现，在七年内，孤独的成年人死亡的可能性比那些感到有联系的人高26%。反过来也一样：好朋友能帮助我们更快康复，更好地应对压力。友谊似乎不是奢侈品，而是像食物和水一样的基本需求。

paragraphs.en: But if friendship is so important, why do so many of us let it slide? The answer is that modern life makes friendship feel optional. We move to new cities, change jobs, and get busy with work and family. A 2021 survey in the United States found that 12 percent of adults reported having no close friends at all. That number had tripled since 1990. We also confuse digital connection with real friendship. Liking someone's photo is not the same as sitting across from them and listening. Researchers say that to maintain a friendship, you need face-to-face time, ideally once a week. A text message is nice, but it does not build the same trust.
paragraphs.zh: 但如果友谊如此重要，为什么我们许多人却让它慢慢消失？答案是现代生活让友谊显得可有可无。我们搬到新城市，换工作，忙于工作和家庭。2021年美国的一项调查发现，12%的成年人报告说自己根本没有亲密朋友。这个数字自1990年以来增加了两倍。我们还把数字联系与真正的友谊混为一谈。给别人照片点赞，和坐在对面倾听对方，是两回事。研究人员说，要维持一段友谊，你需要面对面相处的时间，最好每周一次。发短信不错，但它建立不起同样的信任。

paragraphs.en: Some cultures have understood this for centuries. In Okinawa, Japan, people form groups called moai. A moai is a small circle of friends who meet regularly to talk, share meals, and support each other. Originally, the groups were for financial help, but today they are mostly about emotional support. Members often stay together for decades. In Sardinia, Italy, men meet at the local bar every evening, not just to drink but to laugh and argue. These daily rituals create a web of connection. Researchers who study Blue Zones, areas where people live unusually long lives, say that social bonds are one of the key reasons for their longevity.
paragraphs.zh: 有些文化几个世纪以来就明白这一点。在日本冲绳，人们组成称为“模合”的团体。模合是一个小型朋友圈，定期聚会聊天、分享食物、互相支持。最初这些团体是为了经济互助，但如今主要是情感支持。成员往往在一起几十年。在意大利撒丁岛，男人们每天晚上在本地酒吧聚会，不只是喝酒，更是为了欢笑和争论。这些日常仪式创造了一张联结之网。研究“蓝区”——人们异常长寿的地区——的研究人员说，社会纽带是他们长寿的关键原因之一。

paragraphs.en: Building and keeping friends takes effort, but the effort is not complicated. Research suggests three simple habits. First, show up regularly. A weekly walk, a monthly dinner, or a Sunday phone call can keep a friendship alive. Second, be genuine. People can sense when you are only pretending to care. Share something real about your own life, including your struggles. Third, do things together. Friendship is built on shared activities, not just shared feelings. Join a book club, play a sport, or volunteer. When you do activities side by side, conversation flows naturally.
paragraphs.zh: 建立和保持朋友需要努力，但努力并不复杂。研究提出了三个简单习惯。第一，定期出现。每周散步、每月晚餐或周日电话，都能让友谊保持活力。第二，真诚。人们能感觉到你只是假装关心。分享一些你自己生活中的真实事情，包括你的挣扎。第三，一起做事。友谊建立在共同活动上，而不仅仅是共同感受。加入读书俱乐部、运动或做志愿者。当你们并肩做事时，对话会自然流动。

paragraphs.en: Consider the story of two women in Chicago, Ruth and Alice. They met at a community garden in 1985. Every Wednesday morning, they have breakfast at the same diner. They have seen each other through jobs, divorces, and illnesses. 'We do not always talk about deep things,' Ruth says. 'Sometimes we just complain about the weather. But I know she is there.' This kind of consistent, low-pressure friendship is powerful. It does not require expensive gifts or long vacations. It requires a decision to keep showing up. That decision, repeated over years, becomes a kind of wealth.
paragraphs.zh: 看看芝加哥两位女性露丝和爱丽丝的故事。她们1985年在一个社区花园相识。每个周三早上，她们都在同一家小餐馆吃早餐。她们一起经历了工作、离婚和疾病。露丝说：‘我们并不总是谈论深刻的事情，有时只是抱怨天气。但我知道她在那儿。’这种持续、低压力的友谊很有力量。它不需要昂贵的礼物或长假。它需要一个决定：继续出现。这个决定年复一年重复，就变成了一种财富。

paragraphs.en: So what should we do with this information? Start small. Think of one friend you have not seen in a while. Send a message today and suggest a walk or a coffee. Do not wait for a special occasion. Friendship is not a fixed thing that you either have or do not have. It is more like a garden. If you water it, it grows. If you ignore it, it slowly dries up. The Harvard study, after eight decades, offers a clear and hopeful message: the time you spend with friends is not wasted. It is one of the best investments you can make in your own well-being.
paragraphs.zh: 那么我们应该如何利用这些信息？从小事做起。想一个你很久没见的朋友。今天发个信息，建议一起散步或喝咖啡。不要等待特殊场合。友谊不是一件要么有要么没有的固定东西。它更像一座花园。你浇水，它就生长；你忽视它，它就会慢慢干枯。哈佛研究经过八十年，提供了一个清晰而充满希望的信息：你与朋友共度的时间不会浪费。这是你为自己的幸福所能做的最好投资之一。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Friends are less important than family.
Good friendships have powerful effects on health and happiness.
The Harvard study only looked at rich people.
Social media is the best way to keep friends.
questions.explain: 文章主旨是良好友谊对健康和幸福有重要影响，并引用哈佛研究、孤独危害等证据支持。其他选项均与原文不符。

questions.q: According to the Harvard study, what predicted physical health at age 80 better than cholesterol levels?
questions.explain: 第二段明确提到，50岁时对人际关系的满意度比胆固醇水平更能预测80岁时的身体健康。因此选C。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the moai in Okinawa?
options: They were originally formed for financial support.
They meet only once a year.
They are only for older people.
questions.explain: 第五段指出，模合最初是为了经济互助，如今主要提供情感支持。因此可以推断出A项。其他选项在文中没有依据。

questions.q: The word 'genuine' in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explain: genuine意为‘真诚的’，与sincere（真诚的）意思最接近。文章语境也强调不要假装关心，要分享真实的事情。
